name: merge_pull_request
description: Merge a pull request. One this conversation pushed (its head is a commit you pushed), whose checks passed on that commit, is merged at once. Any other pull request, or one you opened with `accept_red_checks`, is put to the person by this tool itself, in a form of its own with "Merge it" and "Not now": do not ask them first in words, and after they chose "Merge it" call this tool again with the same arguments. After "Not now" do not call it again for that pull request unless the person asks. A check still running is waited for, and a failed one stops the merge. `repo` is a repository of your workspace or `owner/name` on the code host. `method` is `squash` (the default), `merge` or `rebase`; with `delete_branch: true` the pull request's branch is deleted afterwards, when it is a branch of that very repository. GitHub's own rules decide too (branch protection, required reviews, conflicts): if it refuses you get its words, and you tell the person; do not look for another way. It needs the auto access tier or above; at bypass nothing is asked.

repo.description: The repository: its slot's name in your workspace, `owner/name`, or its address

delete_branch.description: Delete the pull request's branch after the merge (only a branch of that repository)
